keyframe_review.note: 1961-1962, 187,924 km2 against the Syria infobox's 185,180 km2 (ratio 1.01; the page gives no year): Syria with the Golan Heights, which stayed Syrian to June 1967. The shape holds from the coup of 28 September 1961 ('Syrian independence restored'); until then the same cells are inside the UAR shape. 22 cells more than Natural Earth's Syria and 8 fewer, i.e. coastline and border noise.

1963-1966, the same cells and 187,924 km2 as the 1961 shape. The Syria page's infobox dates 'Ba'athist Syria' from 8 March 1963 and the 1963 coup page gives the same date; the Ba'ath takeover moves no border. Row boundary at 1966/1967 is Cliopatria's, the regime change was the coup of 23 February 1966 (see the ledger).

region.text: Syria, the former Northern region of the UAR

ledger.note: 28 September 1961: a coup in Damascus restores Syrian independence and ends the union with Egypt. The infobox lists 'Syrian independence restored' as the result; by the night of 28 September, 'it was clear that they had chosen independence'. Jordan and Turkey recognised the new regime on 29 September, Nasser recognised 'the fact of Syrian secession' on 5 October, and Syria rejoined the Arab League on 29 October.

1961: the restored republic takes the name Syrian Arab Republic. The page says it 'changed its name to the Syrian Arab Republic' and gives no date for the change, placing it in the account of 29 September; the year is therefore the page's and the month (9) is the researcher's reading of where the page puts it.

8 March 1963: the Ba'ath Military Committee seizes power in Damascus. 'The coup began at night' and its infobox result is the 'Fall of the Second Syrian Republic' and the 'Establishment of Ba'athist Syria'; a National Council for the Revolutionary Command of twenty members (twelve Ba'athists, eight Nasserists or independents) ruled, with Lu'ay al-Atassi as chairman from 9 March and Salah al-Din al-Bitar asked to form the government. A federal union with Egypt and Iraq agreed on 17 April collapsed when more than 50 Nasserist officers were purged between 28 April and 2 May; the Nasserist coup attempt of 18 July 1963 failed. No border moved.

23 February 1966: the neo-Ba'athist Military Committee overthrows the party's old guard. 'On 23 February 1966, the neo-Ba'athist Military Committee carried out an intra-party rebellion'. Not the end of a state: same state, same land, new regime, which Cliopatria's next row (Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party, from 1967, minus the Golan lost only in June 1967) stands for; reading the row boundary as this coup is the researcher's, the page does not say it.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow the French-mandate and 1949 armistice lines; the Israeli frontier includes demilitarised zones: the Golan page says the area 'was partly demilitarized by the Israel-Syria Armistice Agreement' and that Syria held a strip on the Sea of Galilee's east shore from 1949 to 1967.

notes: Written by me-10-k on 2026-10-25 from four pages. MERGE: 'Republic of Syria' (1961-1962) and 'Ba'athist Syria' (1963-1966) share Wikidata Q858 and the same 52-cell shape, and are one state, so this dossier carries both Names under the earlier slug and there is no separate ba-athist-syria dossier. The Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row (1967-1972, Q16243030) is the same state again and is kept as its own dossier (arab-socialist-ba-ath-party); the Second Syrian Republic (me-10-i) and 'Syria' (1973-2024, me-10-l) are the same state too, so the colour agent should keep one hue across all of them (colours.json already gives republic-of-syria, ba-athist-syria and arab-socialist-ba-ath-party the same hex). FINDING: the 1963 coup page's infobox ends the Second Syrian Republic in March 1963, so 1961-1963 is the restored Second Republic, not a new state. OVERLAP: the UAR row keeps Syria inside its shape to 1966; the UAR dossier cuts it from 28 September 1961. The year 1961 is shared (UAR to 28 September, this state after). No territorial events were found for 1961-1966; the 'War over Water' of the early 1960s is undated on the Golan page, so it is not entered as a war. The Israel-Syria demilitarised zones are a standing dispute from 1949 (second-syrian-republic dossier), not a new contest here. Not opened (page budget): the 1966 coup page and the Syria-Turkey (Hatay) claim, neither of which moves a border.
